newsitem.title: USA: Florida budget contains $1.28 billion of new bonds.
newsitem.headline: Florida budget contains $1.28 billion of new bonds.

text.p: The $42.2 billion Florida budget scheduled for a final vote on Friday contains $1.28 billion of new general obligation bonds, state officials said Wednesday.
The Legislature approved the three major bond issues that Gov. Lawton Chiles proposed for environmental preservation, school construction and highways.

But lawmakers rejected Chiles' proposal for $98.1 million of prison construction bonds. Florida has never issued bonds for prison construction and the prospect of doing so this year dimmed when state corrections officials cut their estimate of how many new prison beds would be needed.
The legislature did approve a proposal allowing the Department of Juvenile Justice to join with an unspecified school district to issue $12 million of GO bonds to build a juvenile detention facility.
But the issue is not mandatory and the proposal did not include a source of funding, said Sandy Sartin, one of Chiles' budget analysts.

The legislature approved $300 million of Preservation 2000 bonds to buy environmentally sensitive land. That will be the eighth issue in that series of bonds, which are repaid with documentary stamp tax proceeds.
Lawmakers also approved $478.4 million of highway and turnpike construction bonds and $490.3 million of Florida Board of Education Public Education Capital Outlay Bonds, or PECOs.
Chiles had sought $502.3 million of PECOS, which are repaid from gross receipts taxes on telephone and electric utilities.
But the legislature rejected his proposal to expand that tax to cable television and water-sewer utilities, which would have added the additional $12 million.
Sartin said the final figure for both the PECOs and the highway bonds could change slightly as updated revenue projections are received.
The bond issues are part of a budget agreement that is scheduled for a final vote in the Legislature on Friday.
